newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid to acquire Thrifty Payless for $1.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid to acquire Thrifty Payless for $1.4 billion.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp., already the largest retail drugstore chain in the country, said on Monday it will acquire Thrifty PayLess Inc. in a $1.4 billion stock transaction that will spread its operations from the east to the west coast.

Rite Aid, which was thwarted in an earlier attempt to acquire Revco D.S. Inc., said it will pay 0.65 share of Rite Aid stock for each share of Thrifty PayLess, or a total of about 38.7 million Rite Aid shares.

Based on Rite Aid's closing price of $35.875 on the New York Stock Exchange Friday, the company is paying about $1.388 billion for Thrifty PayLess, the largest drugstore chain in the West. That would price Thrifty PayLess' stock at about $23.32 a share. It closed Friday at $18.375 on the NYSE.
A spokesman for Rite Aid said the deal also includes the assumption of about $890 million in Thrifty PayLess debt, making the entire deal worth about $2.3 billion.
Rite Aid said Green Equity Investors L.P. and Kmart Corp., which together own about 43 percent of Thrifty PayLess common stock, agreed to vote in favour of the deal.
The company also said it expects to establish a $125 million reserve for restructuring and integration costs that will be recorded at the closing of the deal, which is expected early next year.
The combination, the latest in the rapidly consolidating drugstore industry, will create a pharmacy chain with more than 3,500 drugstores in 26 states and revenues of more than $10 billion.

Rite Aid is the largest operator of retail drugstores in the United States, with 2,809 stores in 22 eastern states and revenues of about $5.9 billion. Thrifty PayLess is the largest drugstore chain in the West, with 1,007 stores in 10 states and revenues of $4.4 billion.
Because the two companies operate in different parts of the country, the combination was not expected to be blocked by antitrust considerations.
Rite Aid, whose attempt to acquire rival Revco for about $1.8 billion was halted by opposition from federal regulators, said it expected the acquisition to add to its profits starting next year.

It also said it expects to realise cost savings of at least $65 million during the first full year of operation from elimination of redundant overhead and by more efficient purchasing, which will result in more competitive pricing for the consumer.

"Combining Thrifty PayLess with Rite Aid's strong cost control culture will reduce selling, general, and administrative expenses, and result in significant operational efficiencies," Rite Aid Chairman Martin Grass said in a statement. "Rite Aid's more sophisticated technology will provide significant benefits to Thrifty PayLess stores and its customers."
Rite Aid also said it will stop doing business in several southeastern states, including North and South Carolina, Florida, Georgia and Alabama.
It added that it had entered into a definitive agreement to sell some 200 drugstores in the Carolinas to Thrift Drug Inc., a division of J.C. Penney Co. Terms were not disclosed.
Rite Aid said it will close the Thrifty PayLess corporate offices in Wilsonville, Ore., and transfer all of its functions to Rite Aid headquarters in Camp Hill, Pa.
It said it will provide generous severance packages to all affected headquarters personnel, but did state the number of jobs being eliminated.

Rite Aid also said it intends to divest the Bi-Mart membership discount store chain that Thrifty PayLess operates separately from its drugstore chain. Bi-Mart, consisting of 44 stores, has annual sales of $365 million.
